propositions: Build a seeded-defect benchmark by mechanically mutating real cleanly-closed plans, using the mutation itself as the known label to measure plan-review gate detection power.

Five defect classes are seeded (absent asserted capability, layer-cake split, consumed-artifact-without-ordering-edge, unnecessary mechanism, untagged operational AC), each paired with an unmutated control that bounds blocking false positives.

Pure counting helpers classify_pair and run_validity compute PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE verdicts, treat INDETERMINATE as false-negative not false-positive, and enforce a >=0.20 INDETERMINATE run-validity cap, verified by golden tests.
The deterministic half (mutant corpus, thresholds, harness seams, counting helpers, tests) was built as WIP on branch calib/6982-e2 and intentionally not landed on main.

The ~100-run live LLM batch baseline sweep and its baseline/run-validity/verdicts outputs were permanently rejected on cost and superseded by the standing criterion_effectiveness.py recorder at $0 marginal LLM cost.
History-mining of baselines is dead because only ~4 plan-v3 sidecar baselines exist versus ~200 needed after the impact_model_version bump stranded history.
